title: Desmos basics: type it so it reads it right
hook: Parentheses, subscripts, lists in square brackets, and zooming out. Small typing habits prevent big mistakes.

steps.prompt: From memory: where do you get Desmos on the SAT, and where can you practice on the same version?
steps.answer: It's built into Bluebook on every Math question, next to a scientific calculator. Practice on the College Board version at desmos.com/testing/collegeboard/graphing.

steps.prompt: You want (x + 1) ÷ (x − 3). Which entry is right?
steps.why: Without parentheses, Desmos divides only the term right next to the slash.
Brackets around the top and the bottom. Without them, Desmos divides only 1 by x.

steps.prompt: Which of these makes a list in Desmos?
steps.why: Square brackets make lists. Curly braces are restrictions, like {0<x<5}, and parentheses make points.

steps.prompt: Why type x_1 (x with a subscript 1) in tables and regressions?
choices: It matches the table's column names, and keeps Desmos from reading two letters as multiplication
steps.why: Desmos reads ab as a × b. Subscripts like x_1 and y_1 are single names, and they're what a table's columns are called.

steps.prompt: The pre-flight checklist before you trust a Desmos answer. Put it in order.
items: Check the angle mode (degrees or radians)
Zoom to fit, so nothing is off-screen
Check [ ] for lists and { } for restrictions
Ask: does the question need an exact answer?
steps.why: This is the course's checklist. Run it in the same order every time so it becomes automatic.

steps.prompt: Finding the mean of 4, 9 and 11 in Desmos. Tap the entry that won't work.
steps.why: Curly braces aren't a list, so there's nothing to average.

steps.prompt: You expect two intersections, but only one shows on screen. What's the fix?
choices: Zoom out (or use the zoom-to-fit button)
steps.why: Many SAT traps are just "you didn't zoom."

keys: Wrap numerators, denominators and exponents in parentheses.
[ ] makes a list; { } restricts; ( , ) is a point.
Pre-flight: angle mode, zoom, parentheses, brackets, exact answer?

recall.prompt: Only one intersection is on screen. First move?
